description: Fixed cross-engine comparison cases; expectations are independent of either implementation.

cases.scenario: Mixed 200/205/210/215 lb sets with 3/3/2/2 reps against 5–8
cases.expected: No all-set promotion to unearned 215 lb; safe next step grounded in observed capacity

cases.scenario: 215 lb for all sets at 2 reps near failure
cases.expected: No increase and no accidental repetition of failing loads

cases.scenario: Repeated completed upper-rep-range work with actual RIR
cases.expected: Earned, physical-stock-valid increment; never inferred from targets

cases.scenario: 4 sets with progressively declining reps and high fatigue
cases.expected: Differentiate early-set capacity from repeatable all-set capacity

cases.scenario: At a verified load, sets complete 14/13/12 in 10–15 with actual RIR 3/3/2 and goal RIR 2. Include lifter history, rest and set order, acute/chronic fatigue context, all-set goal effort, missing effort and near failure.
cases.expected: Recommend reps likely achievable at the intended RIR using individual and context-specific evidence. Evaluate 15 on the first set when supported; allow multiple sets or rep changes when justified. Account for later-set fatigue and uncertainty without a fixed one-set/one-rep cap, fabricated probabilities, unearned load increases or issued-target overwrite.

cases.scenario: Generate, accept, issue, finish and correct an individually targeted 14/14/12-rep workout under the original 10–15 practical band, then plan the following session. Include goal effort without extra headroom, unreported RIR with its original goal, missed exact targets within the practical band and another same-purpose training day before cold repeat issuance.
cases.expected: Retain exact original issued targets and actual effort in history, normalize only the approved practical envelope for the next decision, reject unrelated mixed schemes and unavailable loading, allow further individually justified rep improvements across one or more sets, and explicitly repeat accepted targets on a hold without resetting to a generic plan or borrowing another day's history

cases.scenario: Two saved workouts meet all rep and RIR targets at 200 lb, but the athlete revision or approved program revision changed between sessions without changing the exercise ID, rep range, or set count.
cases.expected: No earned step may borrow evidence from a different athlete coaching revision or edited program. Correctly identify the changed source; preserve completed historical sets and do not issue a higher weight.

cases.scenario: Compare the latest two completed, owner-verified training sessions with individually issued exact per-set rep targets. Exercise actual load is uniformly verified, set effort reported, and the original approved practical range remains 8–12. Include a strong pair at 12/12 and a previously demonstrated 25-lb load followed by a failed 30-lb overload.
cases.expected: Earn a 35-lb load review only from two genuine whole-session ceiling performances with actual RIR headroom; after a 30-lb rep-floor failure offer only a verified historical 25-lb recovery for review. Do not substitute current planned load for old issued loading, change logged facts, or cherry-pick older successful workouts.

cases.scenario: RIR missing despite an issued RIR target
cases.expected: Use each completed set's original goal RIR as an explicit progression assumption when actual RIR is unreported, allow the normal earned increment, and retain missing actual RIR as null in history

cases.scenario: Machine requires 5-lb increments; candidate load 159.5 or 38.5
cases.expected: No unbuildable or unverified weights

cases.scenario: Known bar weight and actual plate pairs
cases.expected: Only suggest exactly buildable external load

cases.scenario: Exercise, attachment or Smith absent from selected gym
cases.expected: No gym-incompatible prescriptions or cycle previews

cases.scenario: Custom workout with pinned exercises and myo/drop techniques advances block
cases.expected: Retain author intent and correct warmups, techniques and RIR

cases.scenario: Create, clone, edit, save and resume a completely custom program
cases.expected: Full first-class authoring beyond legacy web workflow

cases.scenario: Hypertrophy block ~30 sets transitions to strength block ~11
cases.expected: No unjustified volume collapse; use explicit phase policy and dose bounds

cases.scenario: Within one training block, an override changes 5-to-3 or 3-to-5 total/direct working sets, with both weeks separately inside MEV/MRV
cases.expected: No unreviewed weekly set loss or sharp weekly dose ramp; apply explicit athlete-specific percentage limits to total and individual direct-muscle work without overwriting authored slots or misclassifying recovery weeks

cases.scenario: A recovery deload removes working sets but retains the same verified 30-lb load while raising the working-rep floor or ceiling (6–10 to 8–10, 6–12 or 8–12). Include increased prescribed RIR and moved sets without matching baseline identity.
cases.expected: Do not approve a superficially lower-volume deload that silently makes remaining sets harder, assumes a new target RIR is measured effort, or compares unmatched sets to a convenient old load. Preserve authored plans and require explicit review; test legitimate separately verified lighter-load alternatives.

cases.scenario: Bench-priority strength block in four or five days
cases.expected: Adapt frequency when approved, with recovery feasibility

cases.scenario: 3–6 day FB/UL/PPL/ULPPL with gym and locked days
cases.expected: Consistent feasible weekly plan, dose and rests

cases.scenario: 40–60, 60–90, 120+ preference and shorter-session request
cases.expected: Realistic elapsed time, preserve safe priorities and approved caps

cases.scenario: Direct biceps vs brachialis and wrist flexion vs extension
cases.expected: Count separate muscular dose channels without double counting

cases.scenario: Low readiness and injured-muscle restrictions during active workout
cases.expected: No contraindicated prescribed work, explicit adaptive substitution

cases.scenario: Finish repeated after lost acknowledgment and process death
cases.expected: Exactly one durable completion, no duplicate records

cases.scenario: Edit older set after more recent workout; inspect PR/Last
cases.expected: Preserve chronology, corrections and recent observations

cases.scenario: A purported complete chronological lifetime history contains valid workouts 1 and 3 but silently omits completion 2 (or starts at 2), while all supplied records and correction receipts otherwise replay correctly.
cases.expected: Reject incomplete global history rather than publishing incorrect Last, PR or progression facts; retain exact complete chronology after crash, migration and saved corrections.

cases.scenario: 4,097+ workouts and correction of a historical workout
cases.expected: No 4,096-record ceiling and no lost or fabricated entries

cases.scenario: Real legacy export with custom IDs, history, bodyweight and preferences
cases.expected: Inspect, reconcile, approve, restore and rollback without lost facts

cases.scenario: Crash/power loss during import and redo before acknowledgment
cases.expected: Crash-safe restore, no dual authority or silent data reset

cases.scenario: After a correction is committed, simulate lost acknowledgment and cold restart. Present a second durable correction with the same event ID, original root and manifest revision but a different actual load, reps or RIR; separately retry the byte-identical original operation.
cases.expected: Only the exact original durable correction may be acknowledged as a replay. A changed payload must refuse without writing the root, fabricating an edit, removing history or changing PR/Last. A genuinely identical retry remains idempotent.

cases.scenario: Under an authenticated athlete, interrupt publication independently after native Finish/correction journal receipt, immutable history shard, segmented root, workout-ID page, receipt-ID page, paged directory and combined root/index checkpoint. Include before-checkpoint crash, lost checkpoint acknowledgment, stale old checkpoint, restored backup and cross-owner access.
cases.expected: Only one complete, same-owner, exact-revision root+workout/receipt directory may be readable or used for Last, PR and next-session coaching after exclusive single-writer authority is proven. Any torn, stale, tampered, replayed-conflicting or incompletely restored artifact must fail closed without dropping or fabricating any workout; exact acknowledged replays remain idempotent. The current candidate-only checkpoint is not sufficient to pass this production acceptance.

cases.scenario: Offline onboarding to plan, logged workout, Finish, corrected history and next plan
cases.expected: Entire Kotlin-authoritative Compose journey works on Android

cases.scenario: 20 original themes, large font, TalkBack, Focus and foldable screens
cases.expected: Accessible polished native experience without feature loss

cases.scenario: Independent coach sees blinded generated program and cycle outputs
cases.expected: At least as good as web across dose, fatigue, safety and programming

cases.scenario: Generated and authored-custom four-set straight prescriptions of 215 lb at 5–8 reps encounter repeated 2-rep/0-RIR results, navigation, unsaved athlete edits, cold resume, corrections, fatigue/coaching switches and next-session reapproval. Contrast with intentionally authored and labeled back-off sets.
cases.expected: All original issued working targets stay exactly 215 lb across every transition until the athlete explicitly authorizes a new prescription; actual logged loads, optional suggestions and named back-offs remain separate. No RIR or fatigue observation silently changes this workout or a future week.

cases.scenario: At one gym a machine chest press has physical A/B stations with different calibrations; switch A to B, edit an unsaved B load, return to A and reopen after restart. Compare with another gym default and prior logged PRs.
cases.expected: Both real machines preserve distinct verified loading, independent historical baselines, unsaved edits, coaching observations, PRs and gym defaults. Never label B a sudden strength loss or borrow A fatigue evidence; changing a source must require revalidation.

cases.scenario: A five-day ULPPL strength block includes bench on Upper and Push with distinct weights, repetition demands, context and subsequent performance, including a missed Push exposure.
cases.expected: An earned Upper bench adjustment does not overwrite Push targets, history or progression; both days retain meaningful lift practice, exact stock rounding and independent fatigue/recovery evidence across blocks.
